You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

(39, [('arc_stamp_motif_on_exact_zero_shape_matches', 'ARC: stamp motif on exact zero-shape matches', "For ARC grids with a sparse colored motif embedded in a noisy 0/background-color field, a task may ask to find every translation where the motif's colored-cell mask lands entirely on zeros, then recolor those zero cells with the motif color. Preserve the original motif and every nonmatching cell. Match the original orientation only; do not rotate or reflect unless demos show otherwise. Ignore motif bounding-box cells that are not colored: the match condition is that all motif cells land on 0, not that the whole bounding box matches a fixed pattern. Overlapping matches should produce the union of their motif cells. Demonstrated with a 3-colored 4x5 mask: two same-orientation placements on zeros were recolored, including overlaps, and output differences exactly equaled the union. Another 6-cell 1 mask in a 0/9 field had three placements; the output was the motif color at all their cells. Previous examples also confirmed no rotated/reflected matches. Use demos to verify target background, motif color, and whether orientation changes are allowed. Practical caution: transcribing a grid with even one omitted cell can hide a valid match and produce an invalid-sized output; verify every row has the stated width before matching and before submission. Confirmed again in task-58fa3f1c: a sparse 8-cell color-5 mask in a noisy 0/9 grid had exactly two translations whose mask cells were all 0; stamp 5 on both, preserve the original motif and all other cells.

Another accepted instance (task-58fa3f1c): on a 29x11 grid with background 6, scattered zero cells, and an 8-shaped L triomino with mask offsets {(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)}, the rule was to stamp 8 over every translation whose three mask positions were all originally 0. There were 25 placements; preserve all 6s and unmatched 0s and take the union if placements overlap. This confirms the rule also applies when the nonzero background is 6 and the motif has only three colored cells. Compute matches from the original grid, not incrementally from already-stamped cells.

Additional accepted instance (task-58fa3f1c, 16x18): background 0 with scattered color-3 noise and a 7-cell color-2 stencil. In its 3x4 bounding box, the stencil mask offsets (0-indexed) are {(0,0),(0,2),(0,3),(1,1),(1,3),(2,1),(2,2)}. There were 22 placements, with top-lefts (0,7),(0,9),(0,12),(1,3),(1,10),(1,11),(1,12),(3,1),(3,13),(4,2),(5,8),(7,5),(8,0),(8,1),(9,0),(9,1),(11,5),(12,6),(12,7),(12,8),(12,9),(13,6). Recolor the union of their mask cells to 2, preserving original stencil, color-3 noise, and unmatched zeros. Accepted first submission. Reinforces the same-orientation, original-grid mask match across another nonzero stencil color and a denser/asymmetric mask.

Accepted test (task-58fa3f1c, 13x13): background 8, zero target cells, and a 5-cell color-5 stencil with offsets {(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,1),(2,1)} (a top horizontal bar with a two-cell stem below its center). Search original grid for translations whose five mask cells are all 0, ignoring other cells in the 3x3 bounding box. Four matching top-lefts were (2,1),(2,2),(2,4),(4,3). Recolor the union of those five-cell placements to 5; preserve all other cells and the original stencil. First submission accepted. This directly confirms the same-orientation mask-stamping rule for a 5-cell mask against zero speckles on background 8.

Accepted test (task-58fa3f1c, 28x13; background 9, motif color 8): The 9-cell mask offsets were {(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(2,0),(3,0),(3,1),(4,0),(4,1),(5,0)}. Search only same-orientation translations where all mask positions are 0 in the original grid, ignoring bbox holes; recolor the union to 8. Valid top-lefts: (9,11) and (14,0). One failed submission contained a single accidental extra 8 at (15,11); ensure the row-5 endpoint of placement (9,11) is at row 14, not 15. The corrected output was accepted.


Newly verified 27x20 test (task-58fa3f1c): background 9, output/motif color 6; the source motif at rows 7-8, cols 16-19 has mask offsets {(0,0),(0,1),(1,2),(1,3)}. Valid same-orientation translations whose four mask cells are all original 0s have top-lefts (2,14),(3,15),(5,1),(6,10),(7,7),(11,15),(14,13),(15,4),(15,5),(15,6),(16,1),(18,13),(21,3),(21,11),(25,5). Recolor the 55-cell union to 6. The first submission used the correct rule but failed because input was mis-transcribed at (16,19): the true value is 9, not 0. Corrected output was accepted. Check source input values against the prompt, not only row widths; one bad copied digit can make an unchanged cell wrong even if it does not affect the match set. Five fresh demonstrations with varying sparse stencil masks/background colors further confirmed the same rule: same-orientation translations only, match on mask cells being 0, ignore bbox holes, take union of overlaps, and preserve the source stencil and all other cells."), ('arc_fill_enclosed_regions_of_line_outlines', 'ARC: fill enclosed regions of line outlines', 'ARC pattern (task-6323836b): Non-background line art may include long stray extensions. Fill only fully enclosed box interiors with color 4; preserve outline/background and open or merely corner/frame-adjacent spaces. Use demos to identify the fill color and target boxes. Across demos, completed rectangular outlines were filled even when one side was the grid edge (e.g. three colored sides plus the canvas edge), while open extensions and regions that only appeared closed at a corner were left unchanged. Successful recurring test: background 2, outline 8; fill exactly rows 5–8, columns 22–24 (0-based), the 4x3 rectangle bounded by horizontal 8 lines at rows 4 and 9, vertical 8 at column 21, and the right grid edge. Example demos also confirmed fill color 4 for outlines of colors 1, 3, 6, or 9.

Additional verified instance (task-6323836b): background 5, outline 7; the closed 5x5 rectangle at rows 2–6, columns 0–4 has interior rows 3–5, columns 1–3. Fill that interior with 4, preserving the outline and the long vertical 7 extensions at column 3 above and below. This exact output was accepted. A fully closed rectangle at a canvas edge is still a valid enclosure; connected stray extensions outside the perimeter do not change its interior.

Fill both clear closed rectangles despite protruding line extensions: outline bounds rows 3–6, columns 2–8; fill rows 4–5, columns 3–7. Preserve the attached leftward arms (row 5 columns 0–1 and row 11 columns 0–1) and the long vertical extensions through column 5 above/below the rectangles. This output was accepted. Confirms that each unambiguous closed rectangular interior is filled, while non-interior protrusions remain unchanged; the fill color is 4 even when the outline is 6 and background 3.'), ('arc_task_276f8e5f_extend_markers_toward_edge_bars', 'ARC task-276f8e5f: extend markers toward edge bars', "For task-276f8e5f, a uniform field has two same-colored perpendicular edge bars in opposite corner regions and sparse cells of another color in the region by one bar. Extend each sparse marker horizontally through the background toward its adjacent edge bar, using the marker color for intervening cells; recolor the original marker to 4. Also copy the row-occupancy pattern of those markers, aligned by row offset within their edge-bar segment, into the opposite edge-bar segment: draw marker-color horizontal rays across that segment from its bar to the far edge on each corresponding row. Preserve the bar cells and all unrelated cells. Demonstration: 15x9 field 5, bars of 8 at right rows0-4 and left rows10-14, sparse 1s at (10,5),(12,3),(13,6),(14,4). Rays from each 1 leftward to the 8 bar recolor each 1 to 4; matching row offsets 0,2,3,4 are filled with 1 across rows0,2,3,4 to the right-side bar, leaving row1 unchanged. Another demo uses left-top/right-bottom bars of 5, sparse 2 markers near right-bottom bar, and does the same with color2. In test task input, rows0-3 col0 are 5, rows6-9 col5 are 5, dots of 2 at (6,1),(7,2),(8,1),(9,1): fill rows0-3 cols1-5 with 2; fill lower rows toward right 5 bar with 2 and turn dots to 4.

Accepted test instance (task-276f8e5f): 11x7 field of 5, zero edge bars at right rows 0–2 (column 6) and left rows 4–6 (column 0), sparse 7 markers at (4,3) and (5,3). Fill rows 0 and 1 across columns 0–5 with 7, preserving the right-edge zeros. Extend each marker leftward: set columns 1–2 to 7 and recolor each original marker at column 3 to 4; preserve left-edge zeros and all other cells. Rows 2 onward otherwise remain unchanged. This output was accepted. The row offsets occupied by the markers in the left bar segment are copied across the opposite segment from its edge bar; original markers become 4.

Accepted 20x19 instance (background 5, bars 6, markers 9): top boundary bar at row 0, cols 9–17; opposite bottom bar at row 19, cols 0–8; markers at (4,14),(7,17),(9,16),(14,13),(17,12). Treat this as the rotated orientation of the edge-bar projection rule: each marker is in the segment aligned with the top bar, so draw a 9 ray vertically upward from row 1 to just before its marker, recolor the marker to 4, and leave cells beyond it unchanged. Copy marker column offsets relative to the top bar's left endpoint (cols 12–17 offsets 3,4,5,7,8) to the opposite bottom bar segment (cols 3,4,5,7,8); draw 9 upward from row 18 through row 0 in those columns, preserving both 6 bars. This output was accepted. Bar segment alignment uses left-to-right offset, even though the bars occupy opposite halves.

Accepted 24x27 instance (background 3, edge bars 9, marker color 7): right bar at col 26 rows 2–11 and left bar at col 0 rows 14–23; markers at (2,11),(3,23),(4,17),(6,23),(8,3),(11,15). Each marker lies in the right-bar segment: draw 7 rightward through the cells before col 26, and change the original marker to 4. Their row offsets 0,1,2,4,6,9 map to rows 14,15,16,18,20,23 of the opposite left-bar segment; fill columns 1–26 with 7 on those rows, preserving col 0 bar. This exact test output was accepted.

Accepted 24x27 instance (background 3, edge bars 9, marker color 7): right bar at col 26 rows 2–11 and left bar at col 0 rows 14–23; markers at (2,11),(3,23),(4,17),(6,23),(8,3),(11,15). Each marker lies in the right-bar segment: draw 7 rightward through the cells before col 26, and change the original marker to 4. Their row offsets 0,1,2,4,6,9 map to rows 14,15,16,18,20,23 of the opposite left-bar segment; fill columns 1–26 with 7 on those rows, preserving col 0 bar. This exact test output was accepted.

Endpoint note: projected rays reach and include the far grid edge outside the opposite bar (but never overwrite actual bar cells); local marker rays stop before the original marker, which becomes 4. Do not truncate opposite-edge projections one cell early.
"), ('arc_task_8b47860a_recolor_5_as_other_input_color_other_color_as_0', 'ARC task-8b47860a: recolor 5 as other input color, other color as 0', 'For task-8b47860a, each grid uses color 5 and one other color. Recolor every 5 cell to the other color present in the grid, and recolor every non-5 cell to 0; preserve dimensions and positions. Demonstrations: 5/7 -> 7/0; 9/5 -> 9/0. Output preserved the grid shape and mapped every 5→1 and every original 1→0. Accepted on first submission. This reconfirms the keyed mapping for another sparse pattern; count/frequency does not determine direction.

Additional accepted test (21x15): input colors were 5 and 7. Mapped every 5→7 and every 7→0, preserving dimensions and cell positions. Accepted on the first submission. This confirms the generic 5-to-other-color, other-to-zero rule.'), ('arc_task_252fc367_recolor_farthest_repeated_shape', 'ARC task-252fc367: recolor farthest copy of repeated shape', "For ARC task-252fc367, identify the large L-shaped marker object (its color is the destination color). Find a shape that occurs in multiple disconnected components (components can have different colors), then recolor the copy farthest from the marker to the marker color; preserve all other cells. The farthest copy may be selected among congruent shapes such as single pixels, repeated irregular blobs, or repeated components. Evidence: demo 2 has two congruent 2-colored shapes and the farther/top-left one becomes marker color 7; demo 8 selects the farther singleton and recolors it to marker color 1. Solved test: marker 2 at upper-right; two identical 11-cell shapes were the 0 block at rows 2-5 cols 16-18 and the 8 blob at rows 0-3 cols 24-26; the farther 0 component became 2. Keep all remaining pixels unchanged. Additional solved test: a 13-cell 1-colored L marker sat at lower-right (rows 19-24, cols 21-28). Two translated identical 17-cell shapes, both initially color 3, were at rows 13-16/cols 10-15 and rows 21-24/cols 23-28; recolor the farther upper-left copy (rows 13-16, cols 10-15) to marker color 1. Other components remain unchanged. This confirms exact translated shape matching and greatest spatial distance from the marker, not recoloring the nearby copy.
Additional solved test (19x17): marker is color 6, a 10-cell thick L at rows 1-7, cols 1-4 (1-based). The duplicated shape is a 3-cell L triomino of color 7: near copy at rows 1-2/cols 1-2, far copy at rows 13-14/cols 14-15. Recolor only the far copy to 6. The near copy touches the marker but is a separate component; compare congruent component silhouettes and recolor the one farther from the marker, not the nearest. Submitted correct.
Additional solved test (24x16): guide is the color-7 L at rows 0-6, cols 12-15 (vertical leg col 12, bottom row 6). Two congruent L triominoes have different colors: color 8 at {(2,7),(3,7),(3,8)} and color 3 at {(3,14),(4,14),(4,15)} (0-indexed). Recolor only the farther color-8 triomino to 7; the color-3 triomino is near/within the guide's bounding box and stays unchanged. Other 8 components and all other cells remain unchanged. Submitted correct.
Additional solved test (20x26): guide is a 12-cell color-9 L at rows 0-4/cols 18-25 (vertical at col 18 through row 4, horizontal across row 4). Two identical 7-cell irregular components (same normalized silhouette) are color 7 at rows 0-2, cols 21-24 and rows 16-18, cols 5-8. Recolor only the far lower-left copy (rows 16-18, cols 5-8: cells {(16,6),(16,7),(16,8),(17,6),(18,5),(18,6),(18,7)}, 0-indexed) to 9; leave the top-right copy and every other cell unchanged. Submitted correct.
Additional solved test (19x14; important guide distinction): the true marker was the large 9-cell color-4 L at rows 13-18, cols 10-13 (0-indexed), not the smaller 5-cell color-8 L at rows 8-11, cols 3-4. The repeated 6-cell asymmetric shape occurred as color 8 at {(13,8),(13,9),(14,8),(14,9),(15,8),(16,8)} and color 7 at {(15,12),(15,13),(16,12),(16,13),(17,12),(18,12)}. Recolor the farther/outside-marker-bbox copy (the color-8 lower-left component) to marker color 4; preserve the color-7 copy. This was accepted. Caution: when both a small L and a larger L-shaped component appear, use the large marker object, not merely the first L-shaped component encountered. Match components by exact silhouette/translation; don't include an unrelated shape that only looks similar under non-translation reflection.
Additional solved test (14x23; 0-indexed): The marker is the color-5 9-cell L at rows 10-13, with horizontal arm across row 10, cols 18-22 and vertical leg at col 18. Preserve everything else. There were also several horizontal dominoes, which were distractors; neither the bottom-right rectangle nor the far horizontal domino was the target. Important: identify the largest L-shaped guide itself and use its color as the destination; a separate prominent color-9 vertical/L-like component and detached color-9 bar are not the marker. I first incorrectly treated color 9 as the guide and both submissions failed; after recognizing the true color-5 L, the result was correct.
"), ('arc_template_replication_centered_on_marker_cells', 'ARC: replicate a template centered on marker cells', 'For ARC task-61c6d636, a mostly uniform grid contains a compact colored template object and many isolated single-cell markers of another color. Copy the template’s colored cells, preserving its exact relative positions and colors, centered on each marker; the marker is replaced by whatever template color occupies the template’s geometric bounding-box center. Preserve the original template and background. Do NOT assume the unique color 1 is the anchor: the anchor is the center coordinate of the template bounding box. Demos: (1) horizontal [2,1,6] template: isolated 8s became 1 at the center and got 2/6 on either side. (2) irregular 3x5 colored template with 1 at its bbox center: each isolated 0 got an identical translated copy, preserving gaps. (3) vertical 3x1 template of three 5s: each isolated 7 became the center 5 with 5s above/below. Accepted test: vertical [7,7,1] template, centered on its middle 7; each isolated 3 was replaced by 7, with the other 7 above and 1 below. One incorrect attempt aligned the unique 1 endpoint to each target; that is wrong. For boundary targets, use the same bbox-center alignment, ensuring placements stay within the grid when possible.
Additional accepted test: background 6; template bbox rows 12–14, cols 5–7, with non-background offsets from center (13,6): (-1,-1)=1, (-1,0)=0, (0,-1)=0, (0,0)=3, (0,1)=0, (1,-1)=9. Nine isolated 5 markers at (5,12), (8,22), (9,14), (13,15), (14,10), (15,18), (19,7), (22,14), (24,21) each received this same centered stamp; each marker became 3, and the original template was preserved. Additional accepted test: background 6; template bbox rows 12–14, cols 5–7, with non-background offsets from center (13,6): (-1,-1)=1, (-1,0)=0, (0,-1)=0, (0,0)=3, (0,1)=0, (1,-1)=9. Nine isolated 5 markers at (5,12), (8,22), (9,14), (13,15), (14,10), (15,18), (19,7), (22,14), (24,21) each received this same centered stamp; each marker became 3, and the original template was preserved. Submission was correct.'), ('arc_task_2fd86235_extract_colors_from_grid_cell_corners', 'ARC task-2fd86235: extract colors from grid-cell corners', 'For ARC task-2fd86235, the input is a large regular lattice: a base fill color occupies broad rectangles; thin horizontal/vertical separator lines of another color form cells; some line intersections are recolored. Build a coarse output by considering each rectangle between adjacent horizontal and vertical separator lines. If all four corner intersections have the same color and that color is not the separator-line color, output that corner color; otherwise use the broad interior fill color. Then trim all-background outer rows/columns (do not remove internal background gaps). Example: a coarse 2x4 intersection matrix [[6,6,8,8],[6,6,8,8]] with separator color 8 and fill color 3 yields cell matrix [[6,3,3]], then trim trailing all-3 columns to obtain [[6]]. A caution: returning the untrimmed matrix [[6,3,3]] or treating the separator color 8 as a special output gives the wrong result. Demonstrations support this: a grid of lines around blocks reduces to cell colors when all four corners match a non-separator marker; blank cells become the fill color. Crop rows/columns made entirely of the fill color at the outer edge.'), ('arc_task_2fd86235_decode_uniform_corner_cells_in_stripe_grid', 'ARC task-2fd86235: decode uniform-corner cells in stripe grid', "For ARC task-2fd86235, the input is a regular lattice/grid of large uniform-color cells whose divider lines are mostly one color. Some divider intersections are recolored with marker colors. Find the bounding box of all non-background marker junctions on the lattice. The output has one cell per lattice rectangle between consecutive junction rows/columns inside that marker bbox.
